37144-observations-on-madness-and-melanc.title: Observations On Madness And Melancholy
37144-observations-on-madness-and-melanc.creator: Unknown
37144-observations-on-madness-and-melanc.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. _To have taken a comprehensive survey of the human faculties in their sound state; to have exhibited them impaired by natural decay, and transformed by disease, would have implied an ability to which I cannot pretend; would have required many volumes to unfold, and perhaps more patience than any rational experience could have attributed to the reader.

arxiv-1410-2334.title: Gravitational Wave Detection with High Frequency Phonon Trapping Acoustic Cavities
arxiv-1410-2334.creator: Maxim Goryachev, Michael E. Tobar
arxiv-1410-2334.description: A 2014 arXiv research paper by Maxim Goryachev, Michael E. Tobar. There are a number of theoretical predictions for astrophysical and cosmological objects, which emit high frequency ( 10 6 − 10 9 10^{6}-10^{9} Hz) Gravitation Waves (GW) or contribute somehow to the stochastic high frequency GW background. Here we propose a new sensitive detector in this frequency band, which is based on existing cryogenic ultra-high quality factor quartz Bulk Acoustic Wave cavity technology, coupled to near-quantum-limited SQUID amplifiers at 20 20 mK.

arxiv-2104-00751.title: Reservoir-Based Distributed Machine Learning for Edge Operation
arxiv-2104-00751.creator: Silvija Kokalj-Filipovic, Paul Toliver, William Johnson, Rob Miller
arxiv-2104-00751.description: Abstract We introduce a novel design for in-situ training of machine learning algorithms built into smart sensors, and illustrate distributed training scenarios using radio frequency (RF) spectrum sensors. Current RF sensors at the Edge lack the computational resources to support practical, in-situ training for intelligent signal classification.

arxiv-2110-08990.title: Decoherence effects in quantum nondemolition measurement induced entanglement between Bose-Einstein condensates
arxiv-2110-08990.creator: Shuai Gao, Ebubechukwu O. Ilo-Okeke, Yuping Mao, Manikandan Kondappan, Juan E. Aristizabal-Zuluaga, Valentin Ivannikov, Tim Byrnes
arxiv-2110-08990.description: Abstract We study the robustness of quantum nondemolition (QND) measurement induced entanglement between Bose-Einstein Condensates (BECs). We consider an experimental scheme where two BECs are placed in the paths of a Mach-Zehnder interferometer, and a QND interaction creates entanglement between coherent light and the atoms.

arxiv-2205-09044.title: Normalized image of a vector by an infinite product of nonnegative matrices
arxiv-2205-09044.creator: Alain Thomas
arxiv-2205-09044.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alain Thomas. To prove that a measure, linearly representable by means of a finite set of nonnegative matrices ℳ \mathcal{M} , has the weak-Gibbs property, one check the uniform convergence (on ℳ ℕ \mathcal{M}^{\mathbb{N}} ) of the sequence of vectors A 1 ⋯ A n c ∥ A 1 ⋯ A n c ∥ \frac{A_{1}\cdots A_{n}c}{\|A_{1}\cdots A_{n}c\|} ( c c positive column-vector). The main theorem gives a sufficient condition for this sequence to converge pointwise.

arxiv-2206-00857.title: Transparent reporting of research-related greenhouse gas emissions through the scientific CO 2 nduct initiative
arxiv-2206-00857.creator: Ryan Sweke, Paul Boes, Nelly H. Y. Ng, Carlo Sparaciari, Jens Eisert, Marcel Goihl
arxiv-2206-00857.description: Abstract Estimating the greenhouse gas emissions of research-related activities is a critical first step towards the design of mitigation policies and actions. Here we propose and motivate a transparent framework for reporting research-related greenhouse gas emissions, through the inclusion of standardised reporting tables in scientific publications.

arxiv-2309-08608.title: On Egorov’s Theorem for Infinite Measure
arxiv-2309-08608.creator: Semyon Litvinov
arxiv-2309-08608.description: Abstract . A simple proof of Egorov’s theorem for infinite measure is given. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification 28A20 1. Introduction Let \Omega=(\Omega,\Sigma,\mu) be a measure space, and let \mathcal{L}^{0}(\Omega) be the space of real-valued measurable functions on \Omega . Let \|\cdot\|_{\infty} stand for the uniform norm in the space \mathcal{L}^{\infty}(\Omega)\subset\mathcal{L}^{0}(\Omega) of essentially bounded functions, that is, given f\in\mathcal{L}^{\infty}(\Omega) , \|f\|_{\infty}=\esssup_{\omega\in\Omega}|f(\omega)|.

arxiv-2311-17126.title: Reason out Your Layout: Evoking the Layout Master from Large Language Models for Text-to-Image Synthesis
arxiv-2311-17126.creator: Xiaohui Chen 1 ∗ {1*}, Yongfei Liu 2 {2}, Yingxiang Yang 2 {2}, Jianbo Yuan 2 {2}, Quanzeng You 2 {2}, Li-Ping Liu 1 {1}, Hongxia Yang 2 {2}
arxiv-2311-17126.description: Abstract Recent advancements in text-to-image (T2I) generative models have shown remarkable capabilities in producing diverse and imaginative visuals based on text prompts. Despite the advancement, these diffusion models sometimes struggle to translate the semantic content from the text into images entirely.

arxiv-2411-10511.title: How quantum computing can enhance biomarker discovery
arxiv-2411-10511.creator: Frederik F. Flöther, Daniel Blankenberg, Maria Demidik, Karl Jansen, Raga Krishnakumar, Rajiv Krishnakumar, Numan Laanait, Laxmi Parida, Carl Saab, Filippo Utro
arxiv-2411-10511.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Frederik F. Flöther, Daniel Blankenberg, Maria Demidik, Karl Jansen, Raga Krishnakumar, Rajiv Krishnakumar, Numan Laanait, Laxmi Parida, Carl Saab, Filippo Utro. Biomarkers play a central role in medicine’s gradual progress towards proactive, personalized precision diagnostics and interventions. However, finding biomarkers that provide very early indicators of a change in health status, for example for multi-factorial diseases, has been challenging. Discovery of such biomarkers stands to benefit significantly from advanced information processing and means to detect complex correlations, which quantum computing offers.

arxiv-2412-17166.title: Second-order sufficient optimality conditions in the calculus of variations Thanks: November 27, 2024. The author gratefully acknowledges support by the National Science Foundation under grant 2031213.
arxiv-2412-17166.creator: William W. Hager
arxiv-2412-17166.description: Abstract Some classic second-order sufficient optimality conditions in the calculus of variations are shown to be equivalent, while also introducing a new equivalent second-order condition which is extremely easy to apply: simply integrate a linear second-order initial value problem and check that the solution is positive over the problem domain.

arxiv-2504-20384.title: FiLA-Video: Spatio-Temporal Compression for Fine-Grained Long Video Understanding
arxiv-2504-20384.creator: Yanan Guo, Wenhui Dong, Jun Song, Shiding Zhu, Xuan Zhang, Hanqing Yang, Yingbo Wang, Yang Du, Xianing Chen, Bo Zheng
arxiv-2504-20384.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yanan Guo, Wenhui Dong, Jun Song, Shiding Zhu, Xuan Zhang, Hanqing Yang, Yingbo Wang, Yang Du, Xianing Chen, Bo Zheng. Recent advancements in video understanding within visual large language models (VLLMs) have led to notable progress. However, the complexity of video data and contextual processing limitations still hinder long-video comprehension.

arxiv-2505-10496.title: CheXGenBench: A Unified Benchmark For Fidelity, Privacy and Utility of Synthetic Chest Radiographs
arxiv-2505-10496.creator: Raman Dutt, Pedro Sanchez, Yongcheng Yao, Steven McDonagh, Sotirios A. Tsaftaris, Timothy Hospedales
arxiv-2505-10496.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Raman Dutt, Pedro Sanchez, Yongcheng Yao, Steven McDonagh, Sotirios A. Tsaftaris, Timothy Hospedales. We introduce CheXGenBench, a rigorous and multifaceted evaluation framework for synthetic chest radiograph generation that simultaneously assesses fidelity, privacy risks, and clinical utility across state-of-the-art text-to-image generative models. Despite rapid advancements in generative AI for real-world imagery, medical domain evaluations have been hindered by methodological inconsistencies, outdated architectural comparisons, and disconnected assessment criteria that rarely address the practical clinical value of synthetic samples.

arxiv-2505-17581.title: MODEM: A Morton-Order Degradation Estimation Mechanism for Adverse Weather Image Recovery
arxiv-2505-17581.creator: Hainuo Wang, Qiming Hu, Xiaojie Guo
arxiv-2505-17581.description: Abstract Restoring images degraded by adverse weather remains a significant challenge due to the highly non-uniform and spatially heterogeneous nature of weather-induced artifacts, e.g. , fine-grained rain streaks versus widespread haze. Accurately estimating the underlying degradation can intuitively provide restoration models with more targeted and effective guidance, enabling adaptive processing strategies.

arxiv-2510-19233.title: Nearly Monochromatic Primordial Black Holes as total Dark Matter from Bubble Collapse
arxiv-2510-19233.creator: Haonan Wang, Ying-li Zhang, Teruaki Suyama
arxiv-2510-19233.description: Abstract We propose a two-field model where the inflaton χ \chi is non-minimally coupled to the instanton ϕ \phi . By choosing an appropriate coupling function, we realize the scenario where the difference of the values of potential between false vacuum (FV) and true vacuum (TV) is maximized during inflation. Most of the bubbles are created at this time.

arxiv-2601-17384.title: The Universe as a Detector: A Quantum Filtering Formulation of the Diósi-Penrose Model
arxiv-2601-17384.creator: John E. Gough, Dylon Rees
arxiv-2601-17384.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by John E. Gough, Dylon Rees. We consider the Diósi-Penrose problem but rather than postulating background gravitational fluctuations, we instead consider the quantum filter that arises from space-time homodyning the continuum of output quadrature described in the open quantum stochastic model presented here. This is described by a quantum Kushner-Stratonovich equation, typical of the form appearing in continuous-time collapse of the wave-function models in Quantum Decoherence Theory.

arxiv-2602-10575.title: MetaphorStar: Image Metaphor Understanding and Reasoning with End-to-End Visual Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2602-10575.creator: Chenhao Zhang, Yazhe Niu, Hongsheng Li
arxiv-2602-10575.description: Abstract Metaphorical comprehension in images remains a critical challenge for Nowadays AI systems. While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) excel at basic Visual Question Answering (VQA), they consistently struggle to grasp the nuanced cultural, emotional, and contextual implications embedded in visual content.

pmc-10669375.title: Automated Segmentation and Measurements of Pulmonary Cysts in Lymphangioleiomyomatosis across Multiple CT Scanner Platforms over a Period of Two Decades
pmc-10669375.creator: Simone Lee, Alfredo Lebron, Brianna Matthew, Joel Moss, Han Wen
pmc-10669375.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). (1) Background: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis is a genetic disease that affects mostly women of childbearing age. In the lungs, it manifests as the progressive formation of air-filled cysts and is associated with a decline in lung function. With a median survival of 29 years after the onset of symptoms, computed-tomographic monitoring of cystic changes in the lungs is a key part of the management of the disease.

pmc-11369337.title: Developing normative values and predictive models for the 6‐minute walk test across diverse adolescent developmental stages
pmc-11369337.creator: Hatem Ghouili, Ismail Dergaa, Amel Dridi, Zouhaier Farhani, Nejmeddine Ouerghi, Mohamed Ben Aissa, Nadhir Hammami, Anissa Bouassida, Noomen Guelmami, Nizar Souissi, Katja Weiss, Thomas Rosemann, Lamia Ben Ezzeddine, Beat Knechtle
pmc-11369337.description: The six‐minute walking test (6MWT) is commonly used to measure functional capacity in field settings, primarily through the distance covered. This study aims to establish reference curves for the six‐minute walking distance (6MWD) and peak heart rate (PHR) and develop a predictive equation for cardiovascular capacity in Tunisian children and adolescents.

pmc-11472376.title: Uncovering conserved networks and global conformational changes in G protein-coupled receptor kinases
pmc-11472376.creator: Min Jae Seo, Wookyung Yu
pmc-11472376.description: G protein-coupled receptor kinases (GRKs) are essential regulators of signaling pathways mediated by G protein-coupled receptors. Recent research suggests that GRK-mediated phosphorylation patterns dictate functional selectivity, leading to biased cellular responses. However, a comprehensive understanding of the structural mechanisms at the single-residue level remains elusive.

pmc-12648398.title: Evidence of spontaneous mentalizing in children with Cornelia de Lange and fragile X syndromes, but not autistic children
pmc-12648398.creator: Katherine Ellis, Jo Moss, Malwina Dziwisz, Beth Jones, Christina Griva, Sophie Pendered, Roisin C Perry, Sarah J White
pmc-12648398.description: It has been suggested that mentalizing abilities underlie the distinct profiles of autism characteristics observed between Cornelia de Lange (CdLS) and fragile X syndromes (FXS) and autistic people without a genetic syndrome. However, traditional explicit mentalizing tasks have high language demands that may mask true mentalizing abilities in these populations.

pmc-12797775.title: Factors influencing career identity in relation to the clinical practice learning environment, satisfaction, and stress among nursing students in the Republic of Korea: a comparative survey

pmc-12961277.title: Toward efficient screening systems for sunflower drought tolerance: a comparative and molecular perspective
pmc-12961277.creator: Malin Alf, Alessia Ronchi, Aleksandra Radanović, Florian Schilling, Kimon Ionas, Boško Dedić, Srđan Bursać, Siniša Jocić, Zeena D. Costa Rodriguez, Serena Varotto, Dragana Miladinović, Renate Horn
pmc-12961277.description: The observed longer and more frequent periods of drought in recent years have drawn more focus on efficient breeding techniques for drought-tolerant crops. Several systems have been used to simulate drought conditions in order to select drought-tolerant lines. However, little is known about the comparability of different screening methods.
